classification.difficultyReason: Verify the supplied zeroes, remove their contributions from the quartic sum and product, then solve a quadratic for the remaining zeroes.

content.prompt: Show that $x=1$ and $x=-2$ are zeroes of $P(x)$, then find the other two zeroes using sum and product of roots.

answer.short: $P(1)=P(-2)=0$; the other zeroes are $-3$ and $1$, so $1$ is a double zero.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=1+3-3-7+6\\P(1)&=0,\\P(-2)&=16-24-12+14+6\\P(-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $1$ and $-2$ are zeroes. Let the other zeroes be $\alpha,\beta$.

Using the sum of roots,
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta-2+1&=-3\\\alpha+\beta&=-2.\end{aligned}$$
Using the product of roots,
$$\begin{aligned}-2\alpha\beta&=6\\\alpha\beta&=-3.\end{aligned}$$
Solving simultaneously,
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha(-2-\alpha)&=-3\\\alpha^2+2\alpha-3&=0\\(\alpha+3)(\alpha-1)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
If $\alpha=-3$, then $\beta=1$; if $\alpha=1$, then $\beta=-3$. The other zeroes are $-3$ and $1$, so $1$ is a double zero.

$$\begin{aligned}P(1)&=3-5-10+20-8\\P(1)&=0,\\P(-2)&=48+40-40-40-8\\P(-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $1$ and $-2$ are zeroes. Let the other zeroes be $\alpha,\beta$.

Using the sum of roots,
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta-2+1&=\frac53\\\alpha+\beta&=\frac83.\end{aligned}$$
Using the product of roots,
$$\begin{aligned}-2\alpha\beta&=-\frac83\\\alpha\beta&=\frac43.\end{aligned}$$
Solving simultaneously,
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha\left(\frac83-\alpha\right)&=\frac43\\3\alpha^2-8\alpha+4&=0\\(3\alpha-2)(\alpha-2)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
If $\alpha=\dfrac23$, then $\beta=2$; if $\alpha=2$, then $\beta=\dfrac23$. The other zeroes are $\dfrac23$ and $2$.
